text.title: Hipaa Phi Data Flow Design Procedure
text.summary: Nine steps from the infrastructure inventory to the Security Officer's signature: draw every hop with its identifier classes, cut each hop to minimum necessary and de-identify analytics and LLM hops, execute or link a BAA per external hop, encrypt every link and store, design the audit event and its store, scrub logs and prove it with a synthetic-record test, assign unique identities and roles with logoff and break-glass, declare retention and deletion propagation, then route to the Security Officer. Each step names the rule it satisfies and the fields of `02-output-contract.xml` it fills.

step.name: inventory-every-hop-with-identifier-classes
step.input: Cloud account and infrastructure inventory; the service's routing table; SaaS integrations (error tracking, analytics, email, support desk, LLM or embeddings APIs); backup and export jobs.
step.action: Create one `hops[]` entry for every service, database, queue, cache, search index, log pipeline, error tracker, analytics tool, backup, export and third-party API that stores, processes or transmits PHI. Tag each with the §164.514(b)(2) identifier classes it carries and whether it is external (r-phi-every-hop-inventoried).
step.decision-gate: An item in the infrastructure inventory with no hop: add it before assessing any control; a hop that touches PHI and is not drawn is a design defect.

step.name: cut-each-hop-to-minimum-necessary
step.input: The purpose of each hop; the fields it currently receives.
step.action: List `fields[]` per hop with a one-line justification each and drop anything the purpose does not need. Analytics, machine-learning, embeddings and LLM hops receive Safe Harbor or Expert Determination de-identified data (`deidentified = true` with the method) unless a BAA covers the recipient and the identified use is documented (r-phi-minimum-necessary-per-hop).
step.decision-gate: A hop whose fields cannot be justified line by line receives nothing until they can.

step.name: execute-or-link-a-baa-per-external-hop
step.input: Each `external = true` hop that receives identified PHI; vendor contracts; vendor plan documentation.
step.action: Link the executed BAA naming the vendor, the plan and the covered service. Where no BAA exists, either execute one for that plan and service, redesign the hop to receive de-identified data only, or remove it. "HIPAA-ready" without a signed BAA does not count (r-phi-baa-for-every-external-hop).
step.decision-gate: External identified hop with no executed BAA: the design does not proceed past this step for that hop.

step.name: encrypt-every-link-and-store
step.input: Network topology including links inside the VPC; the KMS.
step.action: For every pair of hops that exchange PHI add a `links[]` entry with TLS 1.2 or later per NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 and the point where TLS terminates, including load balancer to application and application to database. For every storing hop set `encryption_at_rest` per NIST SP 800-111 with a managed KMS key and rotation enabled, backups, queues, caches and indexes included (r-phi-encrypted-in-transit-and-at-rest).

step.name: design-the-audit-event-and-its-store
step.input: The application's data-access layer; the log platform.
step.action: Emit an audit event on every read, write, export and deletion of PHI carrying identity, timestamp, record id, action and originating system, and no field values. Configure an append-only store retained at least six years and an alert on bulk access (r-phi-audit-event-per-access).

step.name: scrub-logs-and-prove-it
step.input: The logging layer; the error tracker's payload settings; every request path.
step.action: Install an allow-list scrubber at the logging layer, move identifiers out of URLs and query strings, and write a test that sends a synthetic PHI record through every request path and asserts none of its identifier values appear in log, error or trace output; run it in CI (r-phi-never-in-logs-errors-or-urls).
step.decision-gate: Synthetic-record test failing or not covering every path: no PHI flows through the affected path.

step.name: assign-unique-identities-and-roles
step.input: The identity provider; the list of people and services touching each hop.
step.action: Per hop, list roles with permitted operations, remove every shared account and shared API key, set automatic logoff after a stated idle period, and document the break-glass procedure with its own audit alert (r-phi-unique-identity-and-role-access).

step.name: declare-retention-and-deletion-propagation
step.input: Regulatory and contractual retention requirements; every copy of the data (backups, replicas, caches, indexes, exports, derived datasets).
step.action: Set `retention.period_days` and `deletion_mechanism` per hop. Document how a single patient's deletion propagates from the system of record to every copy, and the media disposal procedure (NIST SP 800-88 or equivalent) for devices that held PHI (r-phi-retention-and-deletion-per-store).

step.name: route-to-the-security-officer
step.action: Render the design, validate with `scripts/validate-hipaa-phi-data-flow-design.py --file`, set `review.status = ready_for_review` and name the Security or Privacy Officer. The agent does not approve; the officer signs before any PHI flows (human checkpoint in `03-failure-modes.xml`, 45 CFR §164.308(a)(2)).
step.output: `review` with `approved_by_agent = false`; validator exit 0; the rendered design.
step.decision-gate: Officer not named or validator failing: the design stays in `draft` and no PHI flows.

list.item: Every hop in the infrastructure inventory is drawn with identifier classes and justified fields; analytics, ML and LLM hops are de-identified or BAA-covered with a documented use.
Every external identified hop has an executed BAA naming plan and service; every link is TLS 1.2+; every store is KMS-encrypted with rotation.
Audit events carry identity, timestamp, record id, action and source into an append-only store kept six years; the synthetic-record test runs in CI and passes.
No shared accounts; roles per hop; automatic logoff; break-glass with alert; retention and deletion propagation per store.
`review.status = ready_for_review` with the Security Officer named; the agent has not approved.
